statement: STREAM (stream-layout-v1) is a second physical organization of the same EAM: the writer needs only Write, the reader only Read, it carries no Index, never patches emitted bytes, and declares each semantic fact once. One validated model yields identical LAI, PCR and AUX under STREAM and INDEXED; only PCI differs.
research_needed: Replicate LAI/PCR/AUX equivalence across platforms, codec library versions and large real corpora.

statement: STREAM body order: 256-byte preamble (layout STREAM, declares stream_dedup_window); TRANSFORM_PLANS; optional DICTIONARIES and CHUNK_GROUPS (cross-file-compression-v1); optional RECONSTRUCTION_DATA; optional RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS; interleaved CHUNK_FRAME runs each followed by ContentObject MANIFEST_RECORDs; Entry MANIFEST_RECORDs; FIDELITY; DESCRIPTOR; 128-byte self-locating footer.

Every STREAM_BODY item starts with a 16-byte tagged header. A CHUNK_FRAME item has no length prefix: its embedded EBCH frame header is the sole authority for stored length. Every other item is a record item declaring a u64 payload length and SHA-256 payload digest exactly once.
STREAM framing constants: item magic 'EBI1', item header 16 bytes, STREAM footer length equals INDEXED FOOTER_LEN (128), record-item prefix 40 bytes (u64 length plus 32-byte SHA-256), item version 1.
evidence_in_source: code; tests: tests/stream_layout.rs item walker helpers (L854+) use STREAM_ITEM_MAGIC/STREAM_ITEM_HEADER_LEN

statement: StreamItemTag wire discriminants are frozen by stream-layout-v1: TransformPlans=1, Dictionaries=2, ChunkGroups=3, ReconstructionData=4, ReconstructionRegions=5, ChunkFrame=6, ManifestRecord=7, Fidelity=8, Descriptor=9.

A STREAM reader refuses any unknown item tag as Unsupported EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE instead of skipping it; stream-layout-v1 defines no ignorable or optional extension item class, so any new item kind requires a new incompatible feature.
research_needed: Format-evolution analysis: how later STREAM versions add items without breaking deployed v1 readers.
decision_needed: Should a future STREAM version reserve a skippable/optional item tag range?

statement: Items follow a monotone canonical stage order (plans 1, dictionaries 2, groups 3, reconstruction data 4, regions 5, chunk frames and manifest records share stage 6, fidelity 7, descriptor 8). An earlier-stage item after a later one is Nonconforming EB_ECF_STREAM_ITEM_ORDERING; a repeated singleton is EB_ECF_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_DECLARATION.

Dictionaries and ChunkGroups items are permitted and required only with cross-file-compression-v1, ReconstructionData only with the reconstructive feature, ReconstructionRegions only with whole-object reconstruction; TransformPlans, Fidelity and Descriptor are always required. Undeclared-feature items are Nonconforming; missing required items fail at EOF.
CHUNK_FRAME items and ContentObject manifest records may not appear after the first Entry manifest record; violations are Nonconforming EB_ECF_STREAM_ITEM_ORDERING.

StreamWindow producer policy: Ceiling(n) refuses a physical organization needing more than n historical Chunks; Auto accepts and declares exactly the minimum required. The library default is Ceiling(0), forbidding any cross-object historical dependency.

The writer always declares the exact window its organization needs, even under a larger ceiling; if the need exceeds the ceiling it fails PolicyRefused EB_ECF_STREAM_WINDOW_EXCEEDED naming the required window, never silently raising the window or rewriting the plan.

CLI pack --layout stream defaults to StreamWindow::default() = Ceiling(0), so archives with cross-file dedup or bounded-lookback groups fail unless --stream-window auto is given, while repack defaults to Auto. Defaults for the same physical decision are inconsistent.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md L195-208 (default 0 for explicit STREAM packing)
research_needed: Usability study: frequency of STREAM pack failures with default window on real directory trees; reader memory impact of auto windows.
decision_needed: Should pack and repack share one default stream window (0 or auto)?

statement: StreamWriteOptions.budget_declared defaults to true. A producer unable to measure output first sets false; the preamble budget is then all-zero, the reader bounds the pass with its own policy, and final actual totals come from the footer.
encode_stream returns StreamWriteSummary: canonical archive, IdentitySet including PCI, total_len, body_len, chunk_frames, manifest_records, declared dedup_window and budget_declared.

StreamContentPolicy: Verify verifies each Chunk on arrival and retains only the declared window (verify, list, inspect); Stage stages every Chunk for later materialization (extraction); Retain stages then places all plaintext back into the model (explain).
StreamAccessProfile::SEQUENTIAL states capability explicitly: random_entry_lookup false, entry cursor Sequential, listing requires a full scan, and the source is not replayable.

STREAM offers no random entry lookup, no partial extraction and no source replay; any per-entry question requires a complete sequential scan, and a piped archive must be re-piped to answer a second question.
decision_needed: Is sequential-only STREAM acceptable for V1, or should a seekable STREAM file support an index-building scan for per-entry reads?

statement: StreamReport exposes declared window, budget_declared, actual entry/logical-byte/chunk counts, frame and record counts, body and total lengths, peak retained Chunks, peak resident staging bytes, spilled staging bytes, the access profile and whether plaintext was retained.

SequentialLimits bundles caller-owned ResourceBudget, DecodeRequirements, StagingLimits, max_item_bytes (largest buffered item payload), max_container_bytes (largest total container consumed) and the content policy.

Bootstrap sequential limits are labelled deliberately generous for the experimental CLI: staging 256 MiB resident and 64 GiB total, max item 4 GiB, max container 256 GiB, content policy Verify, plus bootstrap resource and decode policies. No measurement justifies these values.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS, staging spill and item sizes on representative and adversarial archives to calibrate defaults.
decision_needed: What V1 default sequential limits should CLI and library ship?

statement: STREAM emission is object-major: ContentObjects are visited in logical-digest order and each object's not-yet-emitted Chunks are written immediately before its record; a bounded-lookback ChunkGroup is emitted as one contiguous run in physical_order when its first member is needed.

A grouped Chunk must be emitted inside its group's contiguous run; a Chunk claiming a group but absent from that run, or a missing group, is Nonconforming (InvalidGroupReference), because out-of-run emission breaks bounded-lookback decoder contiguity.
Chunks referenced by no ContentObject still receive frames appended after all object runs; the writer never silently drops a Chunk, though the model is said not to create such Chunks.

Window computation: objects whose runs end at the same frame count form one run sharing S(o); any referenced Chunk with ordinal below the run start contributes distance run_start minus ordinal; the maximum distance is the organization's required window.

Frames are ordered by ContentObject digest and every Entry record (paths) is emitted only after all Chunk data, so a sequential extractor cannot materialize any file before EOF and must stage the whole archive plaintext; tar-like incremental extraction is structurally impossible in stream-layout-v1.
research_needed: Measure staging disk/memory and time-to-first-file for large STREAM extractions versus tar/zstd pipelines.
decision_needed: Should a future STREAM variant allow verified per-object incremental materialization?

statement: encode_stream forces layout STREAM, sets FEATURE_STREAM_LAYOUT_V1 (incompat bit 4), resets the window to zero, validates the EAM, TransformPlans and feature model, and refuses Unsupported any plan requiring undeclared incompat feature bits.

STREAM is implemented only for unencrypted Complete archives: the writer emits no crypto envelope, the reader assumes role Complete, and a descriptor with extension declarations, a non-v1 identity profile or non-SHA-256 digest is refused Unsupported. Encrypted STREAM creation is refused by the CLI.
decision_needed: Is an encrypted or signed STREAM layout required for V1?

statement: The writer clones the entire input Archive, including Chunk plaintext, and apply_native_identities produces a further canonical copy; writer memory is proportional to the archive and the API is not an incremental producer.
research_needed: Measure writer peak RSS versus archive size; evaluate an incremental producer API.
decision_needed: Must V1 provide a bounded-memory STREAM producer?

statement: With budget_declared, the writer encodes every Chunk frame first and buffers all encoded frames in memory to learn stored lengths before emitting the preamble; without it, frames are encoded one at a time during emission.
research_needed: Quantify memory cost of pre-encoding for large archives.

statement: The STREAM DESCRIPTOR payload carries namespace, identity_profile 1, digest_algorithm 1, planner_id, chunker_id, LAI, PCR and AUX with no declarations; normalize_descriptor records layout STREAM, budget_declared and the declared window.

The FIDELITY item payload concatenates the encoded FidelityReport, then an optional ConversionProvenance record, then an optional LegacyPreservation record, gated on read by their incompat feature bits.
The STREAM preamble is emitted with a zero footer hint because nothing is back-patched; the footer is found at EOF, and the writer re-encodes the preamble to compute its SHA-256 footer binding.

STREAM footer (128 bytes): shared INDEXED footer magic, total length, DESCRIPTOR item offset and length, STREAM_BODY length, actual unique Chunk count, actual entry count, actual total logical bytes, SHA-256 of preamble, SHA-256 of STREAM_BODY.

PCI is SHA-256 of every emitted container byte, computed while writing; the returned model records physical_order in emission order and an Index marked not present, not valid, with locators and status 'not applicable'.

The sequential source loops over short reads and retries Interrupted, so one-byte pipes behave like full reads; payloads are read in 1 MiB steps after a length check; consumption beyond max_container_bytes fails PolicyRefused EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT.
Each record item payload and each Chunk frame's stored bytes are buffered completely in memory before verification, so per-item memory is bounded only by max_item_bytes (4 GiB in bootstrap limits).
research_needed: Measure worst-case per-item allocation with maximal Chunk and manifest items.

statement: Public STREAM reader entry points: open_stream (bootstrap limits), open_stream_with_policy (caller budget), verify_stream, verify_stream_with_limits, and open_stream_with_limits, which runs one complete non-seeking pass.

The reader claims it never holds the whole archive in memory, yet it retains every Entry, ContentObject, Chunk header, locator and frame-index entry until EOF, and Retain puts all plaintext in RAM; metadata memory grows with entry and Chunk counts.
research_needed: Measure reader RSS for 1M entries / 4M Chunks under Verify, Stage and Retain.
decision_needed: Is O(entries+chunks) metadata retention acceptable for V1 STREAM verification?

statement: The sequential reader refuses an INDEXED preamble as Unsupported EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE directing callers to the random-access reader; a short input with wrong magic is EB BadMagic, otherwise truncation inside the preamble is TRUNCATED.

Before any payload the reader enforces declared decode requirements against caller decode policy; a declared budget must fit caller policy and becomes the bound in force; an undeclared budget must be encoded as all zeros (else noncanonical) and caller policy becomes the bound.

At every item boundary the reader accepts either footer magic or 'EBI1'; anything else is Corrupt EB_ECF_STREAM_ITEM_ORDERING. Item version must be 1 and header bytes 8-15 zero, else Nonconforming noncanonical.
A record item longer than max_item_bytes is PolicyRefused EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT; a payload whose SHA-256 differs from its declared digest is Corrupt EB_ECF_SECTION_DIGEST_MISMATCH before decoding.

TRANSFORM_PLANS payloads are decoded with the v3 encoding when whole-object reconstruction is declared, v2 when reconstructive transforms are declared, otherwise v1 with an optional codec-transform flag, and validated before any Chunk.
Dictionaries are validated with validate_dictionary on arrival, whereas ChunkGroups are only decoded on arrival and their consistency is checked later per Chunk and at EOF.

For each Chunk frame the reader refuses duplicate Chunk IDs (noncanonical), enforces per-Chunk logical length and expansion ratio against the bound in force, refuses stored_len above max_item_bytes, and refuses a frame count above the bound's chunk_count (PolicyRefused).

Every non-region-owned Chunk is decoded and its plaintext SHA-256 compared to its Chunk ID on arrival, before staging; mismatch is Corrupt EB ChunkDigestMismatch, or ReconstructedDigestMismatch when the plan has a reconstruction step.

Region-owned Chunk frames carry no ordinary payload; because membership is known only from the ContentObject record, whole-object regions are reconstructed when that record arrives and every member is verified before staging.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md §Supporting decoder data before use L266-273
evidence_in_source: code; tests: tests/jpeg_whole_object.rs (L258-302, encode_stream Auto + open_stream_with_limits Retain, corrupted stream rejected)

statement: In STREAM a prefix-coded Chunk must carry group_ref, its group must exist and match the plan lookback (EB_CODEC_LOOKBACK_VIOLATION); the reader keeps per group only the last lookback plaintexts as prefix history, and a non-prefix plan with group_ref is Nonconforming.
ContentObject records must be strictly increasing by logical digest; a non-increasing order is Nonconforming noncanonical, and a duplicate declaration is EB_ECF_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_DECLARATION.

The reader recomputes run boundaries; a ContentObject referencing a Chunk not yet framed is Nonconforming EB_ECF_STREAM_FORWARD_REFERENCE, and one reaching further back than the declared window is Nonconforming EB_ECF_STREAM_WINDOW_EXCEEDED.

The reader computes the observed maximum historical distance but never reports or compares it; a declared window is validated only as an upper bound, so over-declared windows (inflating reader retention) go undiagnosed.
decision_needed: Should verify/inspect report observed versus declared stream window?

statement: Each ContentObject is verified at its record: every staged Chunk length equals its logical_len, SHA-256 of concatenated plaintext equals the logical digest (EB ContentDigestMismatch), and the chunk root recomputed from leaves equals chunk_root (EB ChunkRootMismatch).

Only the Verify policy releases Chunks older than run_start minus window, each once; release is disabled entirely under Stage/Retain and whenever FEATURE_POSIX_METADATA_V1 is set, so verifying POSIX-metadata archives retains every Chunk in staging.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md L335 (Verify retains only the declared window) - contradicted for POSIX-metadata archives
research_needed: Measure staging/spill volume when verifying large POSIX-metadata STREAM archives.
decision_needed: Should sparse-map validation be done incrementally so Verify can keep window-bounded retention?

statement: At EOF, for each Entry with a sparse map, the reader reads its staged Chunk plaintext and validates data/hole ranges, requiring the map's logical size to equal the ContentObject size; mismatch is noncanonical.

Entry records must be strictly increasing in canonical LogicalPath order; path depth, per-entry logical size, cumulative logical bytes and entry count are enforced incrementally against the bound in force (PolicyRefused); an Entry referencing an unseen ContentObject is EB_ECF_STREAM_FORWARD_REFERENCE.

At EOF: bytes after the footer are Corrupt EB_ECF_INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH; required items must be present; footer total length above bytes read is Truncated, below is Corrupt; input ending inside the preamble, an item or before the footer is Truncated EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM.

The footer's body length must equal bytes read, the STREAM_BODY SHA-256 must match (EB_ECF_SECTION_DIGEST_MISMATCH), the preamble SHA-256 binding must match (EB_ECF_FOOTER_BINDING_MISMATCH), and the footer descriptor locator must equal the emitted DESCRIPTOR item.

The DESCRIPTOR must use the format namespace, identity profile 1, digest algorithm 1 and no declarations (else Unsupported), and the footer's actual entry count, Chunk count and total logical bytes must equal what was read.
Under Retain, the reader copies every staged Chunk plaintext back into the returned model at EOF, making the whole archive plaintext resident in memory.

Before identities are accepted the assembled model must pass EAM invariants without retained plaintext, sparse-map checks, the feature model, region-ownership equality, declared decode requirements equal to the aggregate of recorded plans, dictionaries and groups, logical-size agreement, and declared-budget checks.

STREAM checks that declared decode requirements equal the aggregate of recorded plans only at EOF, after every Chunk was already decoded, whereas the INDEXED random reader checks before decoding (random.rs L677-683). Whether a hostile STREAM archive can exceed declared decoder memory mid-pass is unestablished.
research_needed: Adversarial fuzz/security test: plans exceeding declared window/working set in STREAM; check per-plan decoder enforcement.
decision_needed: Should decode-requirement consistency be verified when TRANSFORM_PLANS/DICTIONARIES/CHUNK_GROUPS arrive?

statement: With a declared budget the reader validates at EOF entry count, total and single-entry logical bytes, Chunk count, path depth, metadata bytes, maximum expansion ratio, and requires max_key_derivation_cost 0; decoded actuals exceeding declared bounds are Corrupt EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT.

STREAM metadata bytes (manifest payloads plus reconstruction payloads only) are checked against max_metadata_bytes solely at EOF and only when the budget is declared; with an undeclared budget the caller's max_metadata_bytes is never enforced, leaving only per-item and container limits.
research_needed: Adversarial test with very large manifest record streams under undeclared budget; compare metadata accounting with INDEXED container.rs.
decision_needed: Should max_metadata_bytes be enforced incrementally for both declared and undeclared budgets?

statement: Per-Chunk bounds use enforce_chunk_bounds with the bound in force, which reports violations as Corrupt EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT even when the bound is the caller's own policy under an undeclared budget, conflating policy refusal with corruption.
decision_needed: Should caller-policy violations under undeclared budgets be PolicyRefused?

statement: The reader recomputes each Entry identity and AUX digest and the LAI, PCR and AUX roots from verified content, failing Corrupt with EntryIdentityMismatch, EntryAuxMismatch, LaiMismatch, PcrMismatch or AuxMismatch, then computes PCI from all consumed bytes.

A successful STREAM pass reports every VerificationReport guarantee true (canonical encoding, structure, sections, invariants, Chunks, dictionaries, reconstruction, groups, access costs, content, identities, LAI/PCR/AUX, PCI computed) with index_status NotApplicableStream.

STREAM writer output is claimed deterministic: identical Archive input yields identical bytes and identities. The test only encodes twice in one process with the same codec builds; cross-platform, cross-build and codec-version determinism is unverified.
research_needed: Cross-OS/architecture/toolchain reproducibility test of STREAM bytes and PCI.

statement: STREAM writing and reading are strictly single-threaded: frames are encoded, emitted, decoded and verified one at a time with no parallel encode, decode or hashing.
research_needed: Benchmark throughput versus tar+zstd/pzstd; evaluate deterministic parallel encode/decode.
decision_needed: Is deterministic parallelism required for V1 STREAM throughput?

statement: Staged plaintext lives in ChunkStaging keyed by Chunk ID with a resident memory cap and spill to a private temporary file bounded by total_bytes; peak resident and spilled bytes are reported, and staging is released on success, failure and truncation.

Sequential extraction uses the Stage policy and creates no destination object until the whole archive has verified; a corrupt last Chunk leaves no destination, and existing destination objects are never replaced (EB_EXTRACT_COLLISION).
STORE, Zstandard, LZ4 and LZMA2 plans all produce identical Chunks, ContentObjects, entries, LAI, PCR and AUX under INDEXED and STREAM, with dedup window 0 for independent Chunks.
Cross-file dictionaries, bounded-lookback groups, DEFLATE reconstructive transforms and JPEG whole-object regions are all carried by STREAM through their dedicated items and round-trip identically.
STREAM sink/source I/O failures are reported as OutcomeClass PolicyRefused with EB Io, so a disk or pipe error is classed like a caller policy refusal.
decision_needed: Should I/O failures have a distinct outcome class?

statement: open_indexed_random(source: impl RandomReadSource + 'static, RandomAccessPolicy) opens a Complete INDEXED archive metadata-first over any revision-aware source, without decoding unrelated Chunk payloads; RandomAccessArchive exposes metadata(), metadata_report() and read_entry().

Random open requires the source to hold at least preamble plus footer (else Truncated EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_FOOTER), reads the 128-byte footer then the 256-byte preamble, and refuses non-INDEXED layout as Unsupported EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_NOT_INDEXED with no STREAM fallback.

The unencrypted random reader refuses encrypted INDEXED archives with EB_CRYPTO_NO_MATCHING_RECIPIENT, requiring the separate crypto::open_indexed_random_encrypted path; the reason code misstates the cause (no unlock option supplied).
evidence_in_source: code; tests: tests/random_access.rs::http_encrypted_indexed_read_authenticates_without_full_download (L224-259) exercise the crypto path
decision_needed: Should the plain reader use a dedicated 'encrypted archive requires unlock' reason code?

statement: Before walking sections, the footer's preamble SHA-256 binding must match (EB_ECF_FOOTER_BINDING_MISMATCH), the preamble footer_hint must locate the footer, and declared budget and decode requirements must fit caller policy.

INDEXED footer parsing requires footer magic and exactly 128 bytes; declared total length must equal source length (greater is Truncated, smaller Corrupt EB_ECF_INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH); bytes 96-127 are reserved zero; it yields descriptor and manifest locators, entry count and total logical bytes.

Section walk from byte 256 to the footer: under max_section_count; 'EBS1' magic, version 1, reserved bytes zero; IDs contiguous from 1; kinds valid for declared features; no payload crossing the footer; directory ending exactly at the footer; Descriptor, TransformPlans, ChunkData, ManifestRecords, Fidelity plus feature sections required.

Metadata-first open issues separate range reads for footer, preamble, each section header, descriptor, manifest and Index, plus a revision re-check (an extra HEAD over HTTP); remote open latency and request counts are asserted efficient but never measured beyond a 2 MiB fixture.
research_needed: Measure open and first-entry latency/requests over real WAN/CDN versus ZIP central-directory access and other range-readable formats.

statement: Footer descriptor/manifest locators must equal section framing; the Descriptor must be canonical v1 (no declarations, namespace, profile 1, SHA-256) else Unsupported; Manifest entry count must equal the footer; every Entry's ContentObject must exist; LAI is verified from Manifest entries and footer total logical bytes.

The whole Manifest section is fetched as one range and decoded into memory at open, so default policy (64 MiB per range, 128 MiB metadata) caps manifest size; whether million-entry archives allowed by bootstrap policy can be random-accessed with defaults is unestablished.
research_needed: Measure manifest bytes per entry and open behavior at 100k/1M entries with default RandomAccessPolicy.
decision_needed: Should manifests be paged/indexed for random access, or policy defaults raised?

statement: The Index is a non-authoritative cache: absent yields RebuiltAbsent; a digest failure, decode failure or out-of-extent locator yields RebuiltInvalid and headers are rebuilt from authoritative CHUNK_DATA; status is reported per operation.

Any error while reading the Index section, including a caller-policy refusal such as an Index larger than max_individual_range_bytes, is silently mapped to RebuiltInvalid, triggering a full per-frame header scan instead of surfacing the policy refusal.
research_needed: Test an archive whose Index exceeds 64 MiB (about 4M Chunks) under default policy.
decision_needed: Should policy refusals on Index reads be distinguished from Index corruption?

statement: Index validation checks only that locators lie within CHUNK_DATA and are unique; header misalignment is detected lazily and triggers a rebuild, but a Chunk missing from an otherwise valid Index fails Corrupt EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_DEPENDENCY_INVALID without falling back to a scan.
decision_needed: Should an incomplete Index trigger header rebuild rather than a dependency error?

statement: metadata_report re-checks source stability and returns access accounting with no content verified, zero Chunks, and whole_archive_verified false.

read_entry locates the path by linear search over all Entries; a missing path is Nonconforming EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND, and Directory, Symlink or ReparsePoint entries are refused Unsupported EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_ENTRY_NOT_FILE.
research_needed: Benchmark path lookup cost at 1M entries (canonical order permits binary search).

statement: Random access reads only one complete regular file at a time into memory: there is no byte-range read within an entry, no streaming output, no multi-entry or subtree extraction, and no mount/seekable-file API.
research_needed: Survey use cases (large media, VM images, datasets) needing intra-file ranges; measure memory for multi-GiB entries.
decision_needed: Does V1 need intra-entry range reads or subtree extraction over random access?

statement: Without a valid Index, read_entry scans every CHUNK_DATA frame header with one range read per header, bounded by max_chunk_frames_scanned, requiring frame count to equal descriptor budget chunk_count and, for non-extended archives, digest-ordered frames.

An Index-less or invalid-Index header scan issues one uncoalesced range request per Chunk, so default max_range_requests (100,000) blocks random access to archives with more than about 100k Chunks, far below bootstrap chunk_count 4,000,000.
research_needed: Measure scan requests and time over HTTP for 100k-4M Chunk archives.
decision_needed: Should header scans be coalesced, or should remote random access require a valid Index?

statement: read_entry builds a dependency closure of requested Chunks, whole-object region members and transitive bounded-lookback prerequisites; a closure above max_dependency_chunks (default 65,536) is PolicyRefused EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_POLICY_REFUSED.

Prefix decoding needs decoded plaintext of up to lookback preceding group members, each needing its own prefix, so reading a late member of a long ChunkGroup transitively decodes the whole preceding run; inspection's worst_random_access_chunks equals max_lookback and understates this cost.
research_needed: Measure closure size, bytes decoded and latency versus group length for Dense-profile archives.
decision_needed: Should ChunkGroup length be capped or prefix chains reset to bound random-access cost?

statement: group_prerequisites rebuilds and sorts a vector of every Index locator on each call, and is called repeatedly per Chunk, giving O(n log n) work per dependency on archives with n Chunks.
research_needed: Benchmark read_entry on 1M-4M Chunk archives with lookback groups.

statement: decode_one recurses through prerequisite chains, so recursion depth can grow with ChunkGroup length, and it re-sums all decoded bytes per Chunk (quadratic); stack exhaustion on hostile or long groups is untested.
research_needed: Fuzz/adversarial test with maximal-length groups within max_dependency_chunks; measure stack use.
decision_needed: Should prerequisite decoding be iterative with bounded depth?

statement: During random access a ChunkGroup lookback disagreeing with its plan is EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_DEPENDENCY_INVALID, and direct predecessors' logical bytes exceeding group max_preceding_bytes is Corrupt EB_ECF_ACCESS_COST_MISMATCH.

Before decoding, payload ranges for the whole closure are prefetched through RangeSession::prefetch, labelled Chunk for requested and Lookback for dependency Chunks, so coalescing never merges across these purposes.

Whole-object region access requires aggregate and per-region logical bytes within max_decoded_logical_bytes and region access metadata equal to its logical bytes, chunk count and worst reconstructed bytes (else Corrupt EB_RECONSTRUCTION_REGION_ACCESS_INVALID); members are then reconstructed.

Random-access reconstruction of JPEG whole-object regions is implemented, but no integration test opens a whole-object archive with open_indexed_random; only DEFLATE reconstructive dependencies are tested.
evidence_in_source: tests: tests/random_access.rs::random_access_verifies_deflate_reconstruction_dependencies (L367-404); no whole-object random test found
research_needed: Add and run random-access tests for JPEG/JPEG XL region archives, including corruption and policy limits.

statement: Returned bytes are fully verified: each Chunk SHA-256, cumulative output within max_decoded_logical_bytes, chunk_root from leaves (EB ChunkRootMismatch), whole-object logical digest (EB ContentDigestMismatch), sparse-map plaintext validation, then a final source-stability check.
decode_one verifies each decoded Chunk's length and SHA-256 and refuses when retained decoded bytes plus the Chunk exceed max_decoded_logical_bytes (default 8 GiB).

Decode metadata (TransformPlans, Dictionaries, ChunkGroups, ReconstructionData, ReconstructionRegions) loads lazily on first read with section digests verified; aggregate decode requirements must equal the Descriptor and fit caller decode policy before any Chunk is decoded.

Trace purposes are approximate: the TransformPlans section is fetched as AccessPurpose::Descriptor (counted as metadata) and ChunkGroups as Lookback (not counted as metadata), so metadata-budget accounting depends on labels.

Each random operation returns a deliberately partial report: LAI Verified, AUX NotRequested, PCR DeclaredNotFullyVerified, PCI NotComputed, whole_archive_verified false, plus Index status, Chunks and dependencies verified, bytes fetched, range request count and full access trace.

The report hard-codes semantic_metadata_sections_verified true, yet the random reader never fetches or digest-checks the required FIDELITY section and does not verify AUX, so the flag overstates what was checked.
decision_needed: Should the random reader verify FIDELITY/AUX or narrow the flag's meaning?

statement: RandomAccessMetadata carries descriptor, entries, ContentObjects, source length and revision, section count and directory, plus encrypted and encrypted_segment_count fields shared with the crypto reader; the plain reader sets them false and None.
The random reader uses expect() on lazily loaded decode metadata, relying on internal call ordering rather than returning diagnostics; a future refactor could turn misuse into panics.
Range coalescing is only an access optimization: reading with coalesce_gap_bytes 0 returns bytes identical to the default coalescing policy.

RandomReadSource is a public Send+Sync trait (len, is_empty, read_exact_at, revision) with a Box forwarding impl; SourceRevision is Memory{length, sha256}, Local{length, modified_nanos} or Http{length, strong_etag}. Callers can supply their own sources.
MemoryRandomReadSource hashes the whole buffer with SHA-256 at construction to form its revision; ranges beyond the buffer are Truncated EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM.

LocalFileRandomReadSource pins revision only by file length and modification time (None when unavailable); a same-length in-place rewrite with unchanged or unavailable mtime is undetectable, and stability is checked only at operation end.
research_needed: Platform tests of mtime granularity/availability (NTFS, ext4, APFS, SMB/NFS) and concurrent-writer detection.
decision_needed: Should local random reads pin content by stronger means (locks, file IDs, change counters)?

statement: Local range reads lock a Mutex around seek plus read_exact on one held handle, so concurrent reads through one source are serialized; no positional (pread) read is used.

HttpRangeSource::open accepts only http/https, uses reqwest blocking with at most 3 redirects and all transparent decompression disabled, sends HEAD with identity encoding, and requires success, one exact Content-Length, a strong quoted ETag, Accept-Ranges bytes and identity encodings, else EB_HTTP_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED.

Each HTTP range GET sends Range, If-Match initial ETag and identity encoding; 412 is SourceUnstable; non-206 is Unsupported with no 200 fallback; response ETag must match; Content-Length must equal the request; Content-Range must equal 'bytes start-end/total'; body length must be exact.

The HTTP source has no authentication or custom headers, no explicit timeouts, retries or backoff, no multi-range requests, no parallel connections, and no support for servers lacking HEAD, Accept-Ranges or strong ETags; S3 credentials, WebDAV, FTP, cloud APIs and remote writes are outside v1.
research_needed: Compatibility matrix across CDNs/object stores (S3 presigned, R2, GCS, GitHub releases, nginx, Caddy) and failure-injection tests.
decision_needed: Which remote access features (auth, retry, multi-range) are V1 requirements?

statement: Compatibility depends on HEAD returning ETag, Content-Length and Accept-Ranges, and every range GET plus revalidation HEAD re-follows redirects from the original URL; presigned or GET-only URLs and servers omitting Accept-Ranges on HEAD may fail.
research_needed: Empirical test against common hosting of release artifacts and presigned object-store URLs.
decision_needed: Should GET-based probing replace HEAD when HEAD is unsupported or differently signed?

statement: HTTP revision() issues a fresh HEAD; check_stable compares the final revision to the initial one and fails Corrupt EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE on any difference in length or ETag.

AccessPurpose labels each fetch (Footer, Preamble, SectionHeader, Descriptor, Manifest, Index, ChunkHeader, Chunk, Dictionary, Lookback, Reconstruction, EncryptedControl, EncryptedPayload); AccessTraceEntry records offset, length, purpose and cache hit.

RandomAccessPolicy defaults: 64 MiB per range, 512 MiB fetched, 100,000 requests, 128 MiB metadata, 64 sections, 4M frames scanned, 65,536 dependency Chunks, 8 GiB decoded, 128 MiB cache, 4M encrypted segment headers, 100,000 trace entries, 4096-byte coalesce gap, bootstrap resource/decode policies. None is justified by measurement.
research_needed: Calibrate against representative archives and network conditions; test coalescing gap versus request counts and bytes wasted.
decision_needed: What V1 default RandomAccessPolicy should library and CLI ship?

statement: Default max_total_bytes_fetched (512 MiB) is far below max_decoded_logical_bytes (8 GiB) and bootstrap max single entry (16 GiB), and the CLI always uses defaults, so files larger than about 512 MiB stored cannot be read via random access without code changes.
research_needed: Test random reads of 1-16 GiB entries locally and over HTTP.
decision_needed: Should the CLI expose random-access policy options or scale fetch budgets to declared sizes?

statement: RangeSession::read checks bounds against the pinned length, traces zero-length reads, enforces per-range size, serves ranges fully contained in one cached entry, enforces request, byte and metadata budgets before fetching, and treats short results as Truncated.

prefetch sorts ranges and merges neighbours only when purposes are identical, the gap is within coalesce_gap_bytes and the merged range stays within max_individual_range_bytes; merged reads are cached for later exact reads.

The session cache uses deterministic FIFO eviction bounded by max_cached_bytes; entries larger than the bound are not cached, and a hit requires one cached entry to contain the whole range, so ranges spanning adjacent cached entries are refetched.
research_needed: Measure cache hit rates and refetch waste on realistic read patterns.

statement: Trace entries are capped: once max_trace_entries is reached the next read (including cache hits) fails PolicyRefused, so long sessions stop rather than truncate their trace.
decision_needed: Should trace overflow truncate the trace instead of failing reads?

statement: Footer, Preamble, SectionHeader, Descriptor, Manifest, Index, ChunkHeader and EncryptedControl reads count toward max_metadata_bytes; Chunk, Dictionary, Lookback, Reconstruction and EncryptedPayload reads do not.

Range diagnostics: policy limits are PolicyRefused EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_POLICY_REFUSED; revision changes Corrupt EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE; malformed HTTP framing Corrupt EB_HTTP_RANGE_INVALID; but transport errors (connection failures, timeouts) are also Corrupt EB_HTTP_RANGE_INVALID, conflating transient network failure with corruption.
decision_needed: Should transient network failures have their own reason code and outcome class?

statement: Range access patterns (URL, object size, offsets, lengths, timing, request count) are visible to the server and recorded in the local trace; nothing pads, batches or obfuscates requests, so crypto-v1 does not hide physical access patterns (explicitly not ORAM/PIR).
research_needed: Security analysis of what range patterns reveal about encrypted archive contents.
decision_needed: Is access-pattern leakage acceptable in the V1 threat model?

statement: The core entrybound library depends unconditionally on reqwest =0.13.4 (blocking, rustls, default features off) and declares no Cargo features, so every consumer builds an HTTP/TLS stack even for offline use.
research_needed: Measure build size/time and dependency count with and without HTTP; audit supply-chain surface.
decision_needed: Should HTTP range access be feature-gated out of the core library?

statement: RangeSession (revision pinning, budgets, cache, coalescing, trace) is pub(crate); external code reaches it only through open_indexed_random or the crypto random open functions.

archive module public API: pack_directory, pack_directory_stream, plan_directory, replan_archive, unpack, unpack_opened, unpack_stream, default output helpers, list, inspect, explain, archive_diff, archive_metadata_diff, prepare_repack, structured_explain, inspection_json(_with_security), random_inspection_json; encrypted planning helpers are crate-private.

bootstrap_resource_policy, described as deliberately generous for the experimental CLI: 1,000,000 entries, 64 GiB total logical, 16 GiB single entry, expansion ratio 64,000x, 4,000,000 Chunks, path depth 1,024, 1 GiB metadata, zero key-derivation cost. Applications should narrow it; no measurement supports the values.
research_needed: Measure real archive distributions and decompression-bomb resistance to calibrate V1 defaults.
decision_needed: What default ResourceBudget ships in V1, and must the CLI expose overrides?

statement: bootstrap_decode_policy sets 8 MiB decoder window and 384 MiB working set; the comment says V6 permits a bounded 256 MiB JPEG/JPEG XL reconstruction working set. Values are not tied to cited measurement.
refines_or_supersedes: V6 whole-object reconstruction decision (256 MiB working set, per comment L50)
research_needed: Measure peak decoder memory for zstd/LZMA2/JPEG XL reconstruction across profiles.
decision_needed: Are 8 MiB window / 384 MiB working set appropriate V1 decoder ceilings?

statement: Bootstrap total_logical_bytes (64 GiB) is well below STREAM max_container_bytes (256 GiB) and equals total staging (64 GiB), so CLI workflows using bootstrap policies refuse archives above 64 GiB logical content; scaling beyond requires library callers.
research_needed: Test CLI pack/verify/extract on 100 GiB-1 TiB datasets.
decision_needed: What archive-size ceiling must V1 CLI support by default?

statement: CollisionPolicy has a single variant, Refuse (the default): extraction never overwrites, skips, renames or merges into existing destination objects.
research_needed: Usability study of extraction into existing trees (update/overwrite expectations from tar/zip users).
decision_needed: Does V1 need overwrite, skip or update collision modes?

statement: SymlinkPolicy: Refuse all links; Safe (default) permits only relative targets whose lexical resolution stays beneath the extraction root; All restores exact targets including absolute and escaping ones.

Extraction metadata policies default to not restoring: ownership, xattrs, ACLs, Windows security and platform metadata default Ignore (else Restore); sparse defaults to Logical materialization (Restore recreates extents where supported); reparse points default Refuse, with KnownSafe and All.

ConfinementMode defines KernelEnforced and WeakerReported, but only KernelEnforced is ever constructed (archive/filesystem.rs:622); no weaker fallback confinement path exists or is reported on platforms lacking kernel-enforced resolution.
research_needed: Platform feasibility of kernel-enforced capability-relative resolution on Windows, macOS, older Linux, WASI.
decision_needed: Must V1 refuse extraction where kernel confinement is unavailable, or implement and report a weaker mode?

statement: ExtractionPolicy is immutable and caller-constructed without consulting archive-controlled data; archive bytes never mutate it. Default: collision Refuse, bootstrap budget and decode policy, symlinks Safe, metadata Ignore, sparse Logical, reparse Refuse.
EntryCursorComplexity has Sequential and RandomAccess variants, but only Sequential is used (StreamAccessProfile); no public Entry cursor API exposes RandomAccess complexity.

list(archive) returns entries in canonical EAM order with path string, EntryKind and logical bytes (0 for directories, symlinks and reparse points); it needs a fully opened model, so listing STREAM requires a complete scan.

inspect(opened) derives ArchiveInspection from a fully verified OpenedArchive: namespace, version, layout, role, counts, features, stream window, budget_declared, random_entry_lookup, index applicability, planner and chunker IDs, plans, codec/transform usage, Chunk statistics, cross-file, reconstruction and whole-object views, identities, Index status, fidelity, provenance, declared resources and decode requirements.
evidence_in_source: tests: tests/compression_planner.rs (L37, L147); tests/stream_layout.rs (L190, L621); tests/jpeg_whole_object.rs (L225)

statement: Inspection semantics: random_entry_lookup follows the declared layout, never source seekability; absent budget declaration is never a claim of unlimited resources; stream_dedup_window is always zero for INDEXED.
explain refuses when any non-empty Chunk lacks retained plaintext, returning Unsupported with EB_CLI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED from the library layer; callers must re-scan STREAM archives with Retain.
decision_needed: Should explain use a dedicated reason code rather than EB_CLI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED?

statement: explain attributes savings (ordinary codec, shared dictionary, bounded lookback, structural transform, reconstructive) by re-encoding Chunks at explain time with current codecs and planner-id-derived profiles, not from a pack-time audit record; attributions may differ from the planner's actual costs.
research_needed: Compare explain attributions with pack-time planner costs across codec library versions and profiles.
decision_needed: Should the planner record an auditable cost trail instead of re-deriving at explain time?

statement: explain re-encodes every non-region Chunk (sometimes twice) and re-runs similarity clustering, costing CPU comparable to repacking; on STREAM it requires Retain, so all plaintext must be resident.
research_needed: Benchmark explain time/memory versus pack on multi-GiB archives.

statement: Explanation features are gated by planner-id suffix inconsistently: similarity statistics for -v3 to -v6, reconstructive savings for -v5/-v6, transform-rejected counts for -v4 to -v6 (not Fast, via likely_compressible heuristic), but transform_rejection_reason text only for -v4.
decision_needed: Should explain version gating be table-driven and consistent across planner versions?

statement: explain reports that unselected transform candidates and independent similarity cohorts failed to clear a 'frozen gain threshold' defined in the planner, not in inspection.

Cross-file inspection sets worst_random_access_chunks to maximum ChunkGroup lookback, worst_random_access_bytes to maximum max_preceding_bytes, and every_chunk_independently_decodable true iff no ChunkGroups exist; dictionary-backed Chunks count as independent.
research_needed: Validate reported worst-case access against measured transitive closures (see random.rs:792-916).

statement: Whole-object inspection sets jpeg_region_count equal to all regions (assuming every region is JPEG), sums logical, JPEG XL and representation bytes, reports largest region and worst access, and marks independence only when every region spans at most one Chunk.

JPEG reconstruction explanation: gross savings equal ordinary physical bytes minus stored representation, net subtracts region overhead; audit fallbacks counted as not-recognized, unsupported, exact-verification-failed, complete-cost-rejected, dedup-conflict and resource-policy-excluded.
Reconstructive (DEFLATE) fallbacks are summarized as unrecognized-or-verification-failed and complete-cost-rejected counts.

Chunk statistics: unique Chunk count and plaintext bytes, logical Chunk references, deduplicated bytes (total logical minus unique), dedup_ratio_milli = total logical x 1000 / unique bytes (1000 when empty), and minimum, average and maximum Chunk sizes.

Codec usage takes stored bytes from Index locators (a missing locator is Corrupt EB_ECF_INDEX_INVALID_REBUILT) and accounts region-owned Chunks through region representation bytes under the region plan's codec.
CompressionExplanation keeps legacy store_* and zstandard_* fields beside generic codec_usage; LZ4 and LZMA2 usage appears only in codec_usage.
Explain helpers index maps directly (plans[&plan_ref], index.chunks[chunk_id], chunks[chunk_id]) and would panic rather than return a diagnostic if handed an inconsistent model.
research_needed: Fuzz inspection/explain entry points with inconsistent OpenedArchive models.

statement: Transform usage counts each plan step once per unique Chunk using it and adds region Chunk counts per step for whole-object region plans.

CLI random access treats sources beginning http:// or https:// as HttpRangeSource and others as LocalFileRandomReadSource; '-' (stdin) is refused with EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_NOT_INDEXED because random access needs a seekable file or HTTP(S) range source.

ebound read <archive|URL> <logical-path> uses open_indexed_random(_encrypted) with RandomAccessPolicy::default(), writes only the verified entry, and states 'whole archive verified: false'; no CLI options tune range, fetch or decode budgets.

ebound list uses the range-backed metadata view only for URLs or encrypted archives (reporting ranges, bytes, Index status, whole_archive_verified false); local unencrypted INDEXED files are fully opened and verified, and STREAM listing notes a complete sequential pass.

CLI load chooses the reader from the declared layout: stdin always uses the STREAM reader; a STREAM file is streamed; an INDEXED file is read entirely into memory and verified with the in-memory container open, not the range reader.
research_needed: Measure CLI verify/inspect/unpack memory on INDEXED archives larger than RAM.
decision_needed: Must V1 verify/extract INDEXED archives larger than available RAM?

statement: Encrypted repack is explicitly deferred: prepare_repack refuses encrypted INDEXED sources with Unsupported EB CryptoLayoutUnsupported, and decrypting to unencrypted output is never implicit.
decision_needed: Is encrypted-to-encrypted repack required for V1?

statement: prepare_repack converts between INDEXED and STREAM (STREAM output uses the requested window and preserves an undeclared budget only for representation-only STREAM-to-STREAM repacks), buffers output in memory and reopens it with Retain; --index present/absent is invalid for STREAM targets.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md L422 ('no repack command') - superseded by implemented repack
research_needed: Measure repack peak memory (source model, target model, encoded bytes, retained reopen).

statement: encode_stream is generic over W: Write with no Seek bound and open_stream_with_limits over R: Read, so the no-seek guarantee is enforced at the type level; tests drive them with a write-only sink and a drip source returning few bytes per read.
evidence_in_source: code; tests: tests/stream_layout.rs WriteOnlySink/DripSource (L42-96) used across all STREAM tests

statement: pack_directory_stream plans the whole directory into an in-memory Archive (build_archive) and then calls encode_stream; there is no streaming ingestion path from filesystem to STREAM output.
research_needed: Measure pack_directory_stream peak memory on trees larger than RAM.
decision_needed: Must V1 support bounded-memory packing to STREAM from filesystem input?

statement: A RangeSession captures the source revision at creation and refuses with Corrupt EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE if the source's reported length disagrees with that revision's length; all later reads are bounded by the pinned length.

HTTP range bodies are read with a limit of requested length plus one byte; any body length different from the request is refused (short bodies surface as EB_HTTP_RANGE_INVALID in tests, other mismatches as Truncated EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM).

Random open and each read_entry end with a source-stability check (a fresh revision fetch, i.e. an extra HEAD over HTTP), so a revision change detected only after bytes were served still fails the operation with EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE.
